title: ubind + ucontrol move: a logic-bound flare flies to a waypoint
goal: Prove that a micro-processor can bind a unit and steer it: the flare spawns at (24,32), the processor keeps issuing ucontrol move towards (40,32), and after the tick budget the unit is still alive, its own @x sensor reads past the halfway point, and the max aggregate shows how far right it ever got.
notes: The processor reads @x/@y/@health of the bound unit every cycle, so the observations are the unit's real state, not a number the mlog asserts about itself. ux_max uses the max aggregate: it is the movement claim even if the unit later drifts back. Requires a raised rules.unitCap (a blank simulator world has no cores, so spawns would be born dead) -- tools/scenario.py sets it before the scene is applied.

assertions.desc: the processor ran: enough bind/sensor/move cycles
the unit got well past the halfway point of the 24 -> 40 leg
the max aggregate saw it at the waypoint
it flew along the row instead of wandering off it
and not above the row either
the unit is still alive at the end (no crash into terrain or friendly fire)
